strengths: Novel theoretical framework: The evolving exponential geodesic flow elegantly addresses the Dirac singularity problem on statistical manifolds with principled mathematical justification
Rigorous mathematical foundation: Well-structured information geometry treatment with clear derivations, including insightful connection to SLDM as a special case
Strong geometric results: Exceptional strain energy metrics (8.94 vs 83 for MolCRAFT at Q1) and superior bond geometry accuracy across bond lengths, angles, and torsion angles

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Two complementary benchmarks, extensive ablation studies validating all design choices, detailed PoseBusters validation (20 checks), and thorough structural fidelity analysis
Solid reproducibility: Detailed implementation details, algorithm pseudocode, hyperparameters, and network architecture provided enabling partial reproduction
weaknesses: Incremental practical improvements: Vina affinity scores essentially tied with MolCRAFT (-6.14 vs -6.55); PB-Valid gain (93.4% vs 84.6%) is strong but modest on MolGenBench metrics (31.79% vs 23.07%)

Severely limited real-world performance: MolGenBench Hit Fractions <0.01% across all methods; Hit Recovery = 0 for unseen targets indicates poor generalization to novel proteins, questioning practical drug discovery utility

Empirical hyperparameter design: Smoothing schedule σ₁(t) = λ(1-t) lacks principled justification; ablation shows sharp sensitivity (λ=0.1 gives Vina=-4.72; optimal λ=0.2 appears dataset-specific); network architecture choices not justified

Unclear attribution of improvements: Naive EGF fails catastrophically (PB-Valid 64.1%) but unclear if due to singularity, optimization landscape, or loss interaction; no direct ablation isolating evolving endpoint effect from optimization improvements

Unvalidated key claims: 'Modality mismatch' alignment lacks direct evidence (no ablation with independent Gaussian+Dirichlet flows); Fisher-Rao metric optimality not compared against alternatives; evolving geodesic geometric interpretation could be clearer given time-dependence in equation 8
Missing computational analysis: No training/inference time comparisons; 100 sampling steps overhead not quantified; scalability implications unclear
Statistical rigor gaps: No confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars; single test set without cross-validation; ablations show single runs
Reproducibility limitations: No code release announced; inter-loss weighting not explicitly specified; some implementation details (initialization, exact training steps) lack precision

Rigorous and comprehensive experimental validation across two independent benchmarks (CrossDock, MolGenBench) with detailed ablation studies and extensive supplementary evaluation
Mathematically sound theoretical framework with rigorous derivations; connection showing SLDM as special case of EGF provides useful theoretical grounding

Modest practical improvements across key metrics (PB-Valid +8.8%, Scaffold Hit Fraction +0.02%, Hit Rate <1% across all methods), raising questions about whether mathematical sophistication justifies added complexity

strengths: Novel information-geometric perspective treating molecules as composite exponential-family distributions on Fisher-Rao manifold, unifying continuous and discrete components geometrically

Principled evolving endpoint strategy that maintains well-defined intermediate distributions while remaining geometrically consistent—elegant solution avoiding ad-hoc regularization
Rigorous mathematical framework including correct e-geodesic derivations, product family closure proof, and equivalence to Fisher Flow Matching with geometric interpretation of SLDM as special case

strengths: Well-motivated problem: clearly identifies and illustrates the Dirac singularity issue on statistical manifold boundaries (Figure 2)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: extensive metrics, thorough ablation studies, detailed intermediate state analysis, and strong geometric accuracy demonstrations (bond length/angle/torsion distributions)

Strong reproducibility: detailed algorithms, comprehensive hyperparameters, implementation details, training curves, and promised code release

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core contribution (dynamic target regularization via σ̃₁(t) = λ(1−t)) is a straightforward solution to a known problem; heavily dependent on existing BFN/PIF frameworks with the main novelty being the schedule choice

Modest practical impact: 8.8% PB-Valid improvement over MolCRAFT is solid but not transformative; real-world drug discovery remains poor (1.08% Hit Fraction); critically, generalization to unseen targets collapses to 0% Hit Recovery, limiting deployment feasibility

Missing critical analyses: why do geometric improvements fail to improve drug discovery? What causes 0% generalization to unseen targets? No error bars or multiple runs reported; boundary behavior at t=1 still yields σ̃₁(1)=0, questioning distinction from SLDM's fixed ϵ approach
